info.name: R12 FHIR Connectathon — PeRef Guided Labs (Lightweight IG-Inspired)
info.description:
# R12 FHIR Connectathon — PeRef Guided Labs

Participant collection for a lightweight PH eReferral v0.1 workflow.

## Workflow
terminology → validate → create/send → read/search → receive → accept → close

## Design basis
- PH eReferral v0.1 Connectathon Readiness minimum by-hand test
- IG Ana Reyes end-to-end sample case
- June 2026 PH FHIR Connectathon transaction/conditional-PUT pattern

## Lightweight scope
The initiation transaction contains only 9 resources:
Patient, referring Practitioner, referring + receiving Organization,
referring PractitionerRole, Condition, BP Observation, ServiceRequest, and Task.

The receiving Encounter is created only at closure.

All patient/practitioner data is fictional training data.
The PH eReferral IG is a CI/draft build; facilitators should freeze the event build/commit.

item.name: 00 — START HERE
item.description:
## Purpose
Confirm access and configure the team.

This collection follows the current PH eReferral v0.1 Connectathon minimum path:
**create → send → receive → accept → close**.

The clinical scenario is a **lighter, fictional training variant inspired by the IG's Ana Reyes sample**.
It keeps the same teaching pattern (urgent severe pre-eclampsia + BP 180/110) but removes non-essential
observations, procedure, diagnostic report, provenance, and a receiving Practitioner.

Before Folder 04, set:
- `teamCode`
- `referringFacilityNhfr`
- `receivingFacilityNhfr`
- `referringFacilityName`
- `receivingFacilityName`

Do not use real patient information.

item.name: 03B — CREATE INDIVIDUAL RESOURCES
item.description:
## Create each referral resource individually

Run these POST requests top-to-bottom before (or instead of) the 04.01 transaction bundle. Each request creates one resource and captures its server-assigned logical id into a collection variable that later requests reference:

- PractitionerRole -> Practitioner + referring Organization
- Condition / BP Observation -> Patient
- ServiceRequest -> PractitionerRole + receiving Organization + Patient + Condition + Observation
- Task -> ServiceRequest + Patient + PractitionerRole

Unlike 04.01 (a single conditional-PUT transaction), these are plain POST creates: each run makes new records.

item.name: 04 — CREATE & SEND REFERRAL (TRANSACTION)
item.description:
## PeRef workflow steps 1–2: Create + Send

Submit a **9-entry transaction Bundle**.

All 9 entries use conditional PUT (upsert by business identifier):
Patient, Practitioner, 2 Organizations, PractitionerRole, Condition, BP Observation, ServiceRequest, Task.

Intra-Bundle references use `urn:uuid:` and therefore work before the server assigns logical IDs.

**Participant build tasks (per the connectathon checklist):**
- Create a new Organization based on your team name (set `referringFacilityName`/`receivingFacilityName`, keyed on your own `referringFacilityNhfr`/`receivingFacilityNhfr`).
- Create your own Practitioner with a linked, coded PractitionerRole.
- Create a resource for each resource type required by the PeRef IG: Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, referring + receiving Organization, Condition, BP Observation, ServiceRequest, Task.

request.description: Submit the lighter IG-inspired referral. This single transaction creates a resource for every PeRef IG resource type. The response script captures all server-assigned IDs needed by later folders.

item.name: 06 — RECEIVE & ACCEPT REFERRAL
item.description:
## PeRef workflow steps 3–4: Receive + Respond

The receiving facility:
1. acknowledges receipt (`requested` → `received`) and becomes owner;
2. accepts the referral (`received` → `accepted`).

JSON Patch is used to keep this learning exercise small. The IG tutorial also demonstrates PATCH
for state transitions when supported by the FHIR server.

item.name: 07 — CLOSE REFERRAL
item.description:
## PeRef workflow step 5: Close

The current Connectathon readiness criteria expect:
- a receiving Encounter,
- Task.status = `completed`,
- completion output.

This collection uses the receiving Encounter itself as Task output via `valueReference`.
Finally, the ServiceRequest is marked `completed`.
